attempt: S4/S5: a --std 85 program qualifying a name (e.g. a record field OF a file record) under a module combined with Nucleus level 1, accepted by the compiler; S1: a high-level construct rejected as outside 'the highest level'; S3: a boxed (level-2) element mishandled.
reason: S5's restriction is carried by 1985-SR-VI.1.3.2-p1 (exists; cite.py OK 'Qualification is not included in level 1'), and qualification is a Nucleus facility, so its absence in a level-1 combination is that row applied to the combination; S4 ('restrictions contained in one module might possibly affect other modules', cite.py OK) only announces S5. The compiler implements the high level, where no level-1 restriction applies, so no behaviour of it can contradict S1-S4. S3 is notation (the catalog's box field derives from it, a transcription matter, not compiler behaviour). S6 grants freedom. All three quotations OK in p1.

attempt: A program using an ellipsis-repeated format element (e.g. MOVE x TO y z w) accepted or rejected by the compiler.
reason: S1 is limited to 'text, other than general formats', i.e. the standard's prose; the general-format ellipsis is 1985-SR-IV.2.1.5-p2/-p3 (exist). Quote OK.

attempt: S2 'relax restrictions implied by words or elements': a compiler that enforces a format restriction an SR relaxes.
reason: That error is a violation of the relaxing SR itself, not of this sentence, which only says SRs may do so. Both sentences classify the document's rules. Quote OK.

attempt: A compiler whose effect on compilation or execution differs from a GR.
reason: Such a defect falsifies that GR, not this definition of what a GR is. Quote OK.

attempt: (a) Read 'may be facilitated if ... aligned' as obliging alignment of arithmetic or subscript operands; (b) a program whose output depends on whether straddling items cost extra machine operations; (c) unaligned non-SYNC data computed wrongly.
reason: (a) 'may be facilitated' states possible efficiency, and p1 says storage 'need not respect these natural boundaries'; (b) no COBOL output exposes a count of machine operations; (c) correctness of unaligned data is p1 plus the data rows, not this sentence. S2 supplies the referent of 'such additional machine operations' in 1985-GR-IV.4.3.7-p3 (exists; cite.py OK 'are defined to be synchronized'), so 'explains' names a real row; the observable SYNCHRONIZED effects (implicit FILLER, group results) are p5 and the SYNC clause rows. Quotes OK in p2 and p3.

attempt: An evaluation order differing from the figures, or a figure disagreeing with the rules.
reason: S2 says the figures do not dictate implementation; the order requirements are 1985-GR-VI.6.3.4-p1/-1/-2 (exist). Quote OK.

attempt: Any ROUNDED / SIZE ERROR / CORRESPONDING behaviour.
reason: The sentence states only what paragraph 6.4 contains; each option is its own VI.6.4.x row. Quote OK.

Quotes OK.

(ANSI_COBOL_1985.md near line 23037), and the tables are pointed to by the XIII.3.10.6-p1 .. 3.10.10-p1 rows; p5 and p7 restate the PAGE-absent omissions. S2 is the legend for those column headers and adds no rule. Quote OK.

attempt: 'the sequence of LINE NUMBER clauses that may appear': read as a permission constraint, where a compiler that accepts an unlisted sequence would break it.
reason: The permissible combinations are listed by the tables (1985-GR-XIII.3.10.2-p2 'list all of the permissible combinations'), and the abbreviations by 1985-GR-XIII.3.10.3-1/-2/-3/-p2 (exist); this sentence only announces the notation. Quote OK.

attempt: Read the list as a constraint on source text: a clause containing an element outside the list (e.g. a picture string or literal) would then be illegal, or a compiler accepting such text would break it.
reason: The list names brackets, braces and lowercase words, which never occur in source text, so the sentence can only be about how the document writes a general format; the element kinds' source-text consequences are their own rows (1985-SR-IV.2.1.2-p1, 1985-SR-IV.2.1.7-p1 and the others named exist). The SR kind label does not make the enumeration falsifiable. Quote OK in p1.
